A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose to train score based diffusion models with maximum likelihood.

we show that score-based diffusion models are maximum likelihood estimators for the data distribution, and provide a practical training procedure that achieves state-of-the-art log-likelihoods on CIFAR- 10 and ImageNet.
we show that score-based diffusion models are in fact maximum-likelihood models, and that they are competitive with autoregressive models when trained in this way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maximum likelihood training of diffusion models can be made tractable through a combination of continuous normalizing flows and score-based diffusion models.
the weighted score matching objective can be interpreted as an approximate maximum likelihood objective, and that this connection enables maximum likelihood training of diffusion models.
the log-likelihood of diffusion models is tractably computable and can be optimized to achieve state-of-the-art results.
